title: Fixed Bull Seat Shell and Two Axis Pedestal
description: One newly authored complete static mechanical-bull-style amusement-seat exterior. A continuous wide short-neck bull-shaped riding shell has a broad blunt muzzle, two outward-upturned blunt horns, seated eyes, lateral ears and one short hanging tail. Its low concave saddle and rooted loop grip belong to the same complete ride, not a separate animal count. Instead of standing on hooves, the shell mounts directly through an underside stem into a visible two-axis cradle: paired side trunnions support an open rectangular intermediate frame, separate front and rear bearings carry a longitudinal upper shaft, and the whole assembly stands on two rooted lower cheeks and one broad finite base. All new numeric geometry: no old cow moved onto a stand and no spring-rider body or helix reused. The new shell has no udder, weight-bearing legs or biological anatomy claim, and the pedestal has no coil spring. One complete prop zero scenes, four opaque PBR roles, metres Z up and horizontally bounds-centred ground origin. Empty fixed art display only: the separated shafts and support members do not establish a validated motion mechanism, motor, control system, balance, rider fit, load, restraint, operation, fabrication or safety. No person, arena, rigging, animation or interaction is made.
